text:
alice-cust: Hi team — I accepted the org invite and can see the org in the console, but when I open the project it says "You don't have access" and everything is greyed out. My Okta group (okta:team-redwood) should map to project-admins. I tried logout/login, same.
jen-support: sorry about that — can you paste the exact project id and the email you used to join? also any error in browser console? :eyeglasses:
alice-cust: project id 98765, email alice@acme.com. No browser errors, just 403 on every project API call. The UI shows role bindings include okta:team-redwood -> project-admins.
tom-infra: can you run a quick API check? from a shell:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/projects/98765/permissions" | jq .
```
alice-cust: ran that, got 403 with body: `{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "reason": "no effective role"
}`
jen-support: mmkay. tagging infra/iam. @tom-infra any known SCIM/group mapping issues recently?
tom-infra: previous deploy trimmed group names, but we had a rolling window where SCIM created duplicate groups if the identity provider sent a trailing space in displayName. sending quick query to check group ids for okta:team-redwood.
deploy-bot: scim-sync-job 2026-06-02T14:12:09Z started (job id: scim-20260602-4532)
tom-infra: found two groups: `okta:team-redwood` (gid g-1122) and `okta:team-redwood ` with trailing space (gid g-7788). The project binding references g-1122, but SCIM put the user into g-7788. so the console shows binding but user isn't in that exact group id.
maria-iam: ouch. that explains the mismatch. we can: 1) reassign users from g-7788 -> g-1122, or 2) update project binding to union both gids. quick mitigation: add alice@acme.com directly as a member to the project while we fix mapping.
jen-support: alice — if you create a direct invite link in the project and accept, you should get temporary access. want me to send that? :+1:
alice-cust: yes please, that would unblock me for today.
jen-support: sent invite link, confirmed accepted. you should have access now — can you confirm you can open project settings?
alice-cust: yep settings open, can see admin actions. thanks!
maria-iam: going to clean up the duplicate group. plan: run a migration that consolidates SCIM groups that differ only by trailing whitespace, remove orphaned gid g-7788, and add its memberships into g-1122. will run in 20m against a dry-run then apply.
tom-infra: pulled audit info: SCIM events show Okta sent displayName with trailing space for ~30 minutes during a reorg on 2026-06-02 14:00 UTC. we'll add normalization on ingestion to strip whitespace so this doesn't recur.
maria-iam: dry-run done, looks good. applying now. will post job id.
deploy-bot: scim-sync-job scim-20260602-4532 completed (dry-run)
deploy-bot: scim-migrate-job scim-migrate-7788-1122 started (job id: scim-mig-20260602-77)
maria-iam: migration complete. removed orphaned group g-7788 and merged 54 members into g-1122. invalid bindings cleaned.
jen-support: alice — can you sign out and back in to confirm behavior persists?
alice-cust: signed out/in. still see access without issue. thanks.
jen-support: marking as resolved but leaving follow-up to add ingestion normalization and a health check that flags duplicate SCIM groups. creating follow-up ticket: #INFRA-1129.
jen-support: summary for notes: root cause — identity provider sent SCIM group displayName with trailing whitespace creating duplicate group gid; project bound to canonical gid but user was added to duplicate; UI showed binding (so appeared correct) but effective membership failed -> 403. workaround — direct invite or consolidate group. fixes — normalize SCIM names on ingestion, migration to merge duplicate gids, add duplicate-group alert. :white_check_mark:
alice-cust: appreciate the fast help, saved demo today :relieved:
maria-iam: added postmortem blurb to ticket and will coordinate with Okta team to see why trailing space was sent.
jen-support: closing thread in 24h if no regressions. thanks everyone.
